fieldValues.title: check-pr-classification.mjs supports "|" as a field separator, deliberately, alongside "·"
fieldValues.summary: The classification-line parser accepts both 'Mode: X · Cell: Y · Door: Z' and 'Mode: X | Cell: Y | Door: Z' as the same three-field shape. It does NOT try to also parse the bullet-list shape ('- **Decision mode:** clear'), the no-colon shape ('Cell ♑ Repository'), or a line missing the Cell label entirely -- all four were found live in the last-20-PR corpus scan (see the sibling finding). Those are left failing.
fieldValues.rationale: The issue's own acceptance test treats corpus failures as a finding, not something to chase: 'Prove the real corpus of recent PRs passes... report any that would have failed -- that list is a finding, not a blocker.' Supporting the pipe delimiter is principled (same three labeled fields, different separator character, and it covered a whole batch of real merged PRs written by one session in one sitting). Reaching further -- accepting a bullet list, or a line with no Cell label -- would mean guessing at structure the PR never actually stated, which is exactly the free-text-against-a-closed-vocabulary problem srs#716 was filed to close. If a future unit is tempted to loosen the grammar further to raise the corpus pass rate, re-read this before doing it: the pass rate is not the goal, a checkable claim is.
